solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flat-bottomed boat not so heavy

blocks.note: first meaning: a barge used to ferry goods between ship and shore
second meaning: the comparative of an adjective for low weight

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description of a boat that weighs little, but the boat and the comparison are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge for unloading cargo is a lighter, and the comparative adjective also means weighing less than something else.

clue.text: Golf course with large signs in US

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large
in American usage, to ink a deal is to sign it

explanation.surface: An American golf course boasting big signboards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In US' flags the American informal verb: a player who inks a contract signs it.
explanation.definitionFit: Links is the traditional name for a seaside golf course, now used loosely for any golfing ground.

clue.text: Attending pastry chefs regularly failing to cope

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: attending an event is going to it
a pie is a pastry dish
first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Pastry chefs who show up for work keep falling apart under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pastry chefs' reads as one phrase, but pastry gives a dish and chefs is the word thinned out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone losing emotional control, unable to manage a stressful situation.

clue.text: Comb back of mullet with simplicity

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the hairstyle's name
ease is simplicity, lack of difficulty

explanation.surface: Simply running a comb through the back of a mullet haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: A mullet is a haircut short at the front and long at the back, which suits the comb, but here it only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease hair is to comb it backwards towards the scalp to give volume, a verb sense of comb.

clue.text: TV accessory’s key test probing centre of screen

indicators.note: the centre of a six-letter word is its middle pair of letters
a probe pushes its way inside something, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: the two central letters of the word
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British cars
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A television gadget gets its test by poking at the middle of the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The test probes the pair made from the screen's centre followed by the key; the 's stands for 'is'. MOT is the Ministry of Transport vehicle test in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The remote control is the handheld gadget used to operate a television from across the room.

clue.text: Anaesthetic in patella colonel recalled

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
to recall is to call back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An army officer remembering the anaesthetic he had for a kneecap operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' suggests memory, but it turns the letters spanning the two words back to front. The patella is the kneecap.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is the everyday shortening of local anaesthetic, which numbs only one part of the body.

clue.text: Former Republican working afterwards

blocks.note: late means former, as in the late chairman
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An ex-Republican politician who has found a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a retired American politician still employed; each word simply contributes its piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe something happening at a subsequent time, so they are interchangeable adverbs.

clue.text: Line of people cold, on edge, wanting electrical device

blocks.note: a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A shivering, nervous queue of people wants some electrical gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' looks like nervousness but 'on' just places the edge after the cold. In Britain a crocodile is a column of pupils walking two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile clip is a sprung metal clamp with toothed jaws used to make temporary electrical connections.

clue.text: Heave into narrow sled: suitcases, holdalls, etc

indicators.note: putting one thing into another means it is placed inside

blocks.note: to heave or gag is to retch
a luge is a small, narrow racing toboggan

explanation.surface: Hauling all the bags and cases onto a slim sledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heave' looks like lifting the bags, but it means retching; it goes into the sled after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is the collective noun for travellers' bags and cases, so the examples define it.

clue.text: Exotic mineral found by steadfast traveller out of this world

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so these letters take an unfamiliar form

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
strong in the sense of firm and resolute

explanation.surface: A determined explorer comes across a rare, otherworldly mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a space rock found by a hardy explorer, which fits the moonwalker neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The American astronaut was the first person to walk on the Moon, literally a voyager beyond Earth.

clue.text: Kentish chap grabs minute portion

indicators.note: to grab something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: Kent lies in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
a gent is a man
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A man from Kent seizes a tiny share of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like an adjective meaning tiny, but it is the unit of time. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one of the parts something is divided into, a straightforward synonym for portion.

clue.text: German agreed to track port and Spanish wine

indicators.note: to track is to follow behind, so this piece comes after the next one

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A German consents to follow port with a glass of Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as a fortified wine alongside the Spanish one, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Composer and Charlie enter vehicle?

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to hop in is to get into a car

explanation.surface: A composer and a friend called Charlie climb into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that 'enter vehicle' is a casual phrase rather than a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was the Polish Romantic composer famous for his piano works.

clue.text: Chopper used for taking holiday in Cromer’s outskirts

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept
to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the town's name
leave is time off work

explanation.surface: A meat chopper brought along for a seaside holiday on the edge of Cromer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromer is a seaside resort in Norfolk; 'in' looks like a container signal but the holiday sits within the outer letters because of 'taking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy broad-bladed knife for chopping meat, so it is a kind of chopper.

clue.text: In motor racing, a burst’s overcome initially, acting all together

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
initially means at the start, so the first letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: Indy is IndyCar, the American open-wheel motor racing series
taken as written
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: At a motor race, a driver's sudden burst of speed is eventually overpowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like scene-setting at a race but places the other pieces inside the racing word; the 's just links the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means as a single group, with everyone moving or acting in unison.

clue.text: Individual keeps tree burning

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it, so one piece is held inside

blocks.note: one is a single individual
a fir is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: A person holds on to a tree that is ablaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Individual' looks like an adjective but stands for a single person or unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire is alight and in flames, so the phrase directly means burning.

clue.text: Heard enjoyable rock

indicators.note: something heard is taken by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: nice means pleasant or enjoyable

explanation.surface: Listening to some pleasant rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music after 'heard', but it is the geological sense; the silent G is the catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock formed under high temperature and pressure.

clue.text: Heather in charge during long period

indicators.note: what happens during something takes place within it, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge
an era is a long span of time

explanation.surface: Heather has been running things for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' reads as a woman's name in charge, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, so the name stands for the shrub.

clue.text: Disregard false leg caught in fishing gear

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so these letters are rearranged into a counterfeit order
something in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a net is used to catch fish

explanation.surface: An artificial leg tangled up in a fishing net, best ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False leg' suggests a prosthesis; 'false' actually shuffles the leg, and 'caught' is a cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to ignore it or fail to give it attention, a synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Georgia — fine, feminine English bloomer

blocks.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
F is the abbreviation for feminine
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Georgia is a lovely, delicate English flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a flowering plant; in British slang it is a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is British informal for an embarrassing mistake, and a gaffe is a social blunder.

clue.text: Shocking weapon seaman hides somewhere peripherally

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it covered inside, so one piece holds the other
the periphery is the outer edge, so just the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: a tar is an old slang word for a sailor
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A sailor stashes an electric stun gun away somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' sounds like outrage but is literal: the weapon delivers an electric shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a brand of stun gun firing darts that deliver an incapacitating electric shock.

clue.text: African landmark old monarch declines

blocks.note: Queen Victoria reigned over Britain from 1837 to 1901
falls means drops or declines

explanation.surface: An African monument where an aged ruler is fading away.
explanation.walkthrough: The waterfall was named after the queen by the explorer Livingstone, so the wordplay retraces the real name.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfall on the Zambezi between Zambia and Zimbabwe is one of Africa's most famous natural sights.

clue.text: Rugby star, missing half year, out of practice

indicators.note: missing half means losing half its letters, so only part of the word stays

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
the word cut down to its first half
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A top rugby player sidelined for six months has lost match sharpness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing half year' reads as six months out injured, but the halving applies to the star and the year is only its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty describes skills that have deteriorated through lack of use, like metal corroding when left idle.

clue.text: Slippery creature among salespeople lying about earring

indicators.note: something among others sits in their midst, so one piece goes inside
about means turned round, so the whole result runs backwards

blocks.note: an eel is famously slippery
reps are sales representatives

explanation.surface: A sly character among the sales team tells fibs about a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests dishonest salespeople, but with 'about' it turns the combined letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is a small plain hoop or stud worn to keep a newly pierced ear hole open.
